title: Review
description: One review of the future plan: the question the system asked, the options it offered, what the runner chose, and what happened after. A review is an option set with a 'keep as is' first option (docs/ux/review-flow.md), not a notification with a single accept button.

openedAtDay.description: Training day the review opened. One review prompt per rolling week at most (review-triggers.yaml#dwell_days and #max_prompts_per_week).

openedBy.description: User-triggered reviews are first-class: the button exists so a runner can be the one who notices.

evidence.description: Why the system asked, as evidence rather than as a cause: the observations, the rules that fired, and how good the readings were. Renamed from `trigger` on 2026-11-04 - the same object is stored as reviews.rule_id plus reviews.evidence_snapshot and reviews.evidence_hash, and `trigger` names a database object in every reader's head (docs/engineering/contract-vocabulary.md item 3). `openedBy` stays the answer to who asked.

signalIds.description: Concrete observations, e.g. 'rhr_delta_sd:3' or 'feedback:motivation:low:streak4'. Never a device composite (metric-catalog.yaml#grade_gate).

ruleIds.description: heuristic rule ids that fired, kebab-case, so the UI can show which rule asked.

evidenceGradeMax.description: Highest grade among the cited sources. D-graded evidence cannot open a review (safety-hard-stops.yaml#grade_a_or_b_only).

streakDays.description: Consecutive confirming readings; a single bad day never opens a review (noise.yaml#min_consecutive_observations).

horizonDays.description: How far into the future the options may reach. Default 14 (review-triggers.yaml#horizon_days).

freezeDays.description: Tomorrow and the day after are off limits to a review; those belong to micro-adjust (docs/adr/0005).

options.description: Option 0 is always keepAsIs: true. Order is fixed by the engine, never by persuasion.

labelKey.description: Message-catalogue key (AGENTS rule 8); the label is translated, not generated.

diffId.description: Null for the keepAsIs option: no diff, no change, no version bump.

costSummary.description: Stated cost in the runner's terms, e.g. 'the Tuesday intervals move to Sunday and the long run shortens by 4 km'.

expiresAfterDay.description: An unanswered review expires rather than nagging; expiry is recorded, not deleted.

status.description: One vocabulary for where a review stands, shared with the store (docs/engineering/contract-vocabulary.md item 4). accepted and rejected are final - the reviews_one_decision trigger refuses a second decision; deferred means the runner asked to be asked again later, expired means an option set aged out unanswered, superseded means a newer review replaced this one without the runner choosing. Measured gap: reviews.status still accepts the default 'suggested' and spells finality 'declined', and its CHECK has no 'superseded' value at all, so a review cannot be recorded as superseded today; closing that is row R4 of the application table on the vocabulary page, not this file.

resultDiffId.description: Set only on accept. A rejection records no diff but does raise the trigger threshold for the next 30 days.

rejectedThresholdRaiseDays.description: After a rejection the same trigger waits longer before asking again. The runner chose the current plan; the system does not ask twice in a week. The number is not a knob: it comes from the rule knowledge/heuristics/review-triggers.yaml#rejected-review-is-data, whose then: says raise_that_trigger's_threshold_for_30d, and whose explain: key is review-rejection-respected. There is no rejection_cooldown_days knob in that file, and a citation naming one would be a dead link the Markdown auditor cannot see (item 18).

outcomeCheckDay.description: Day the review is scored against feedback, so 'did that help?' becomes an answer instead of a memory.

allowedNumbers.description: Every number the narrative may contain, supplied by the engine. A validator rejects any numeric token not in this list (AGENTS rule 2).

generated.description: False when the template fallback produced the text, which is the normal path for short strings.
